description.text: Masco Corporation and its subsidiaries (the “Company”) is a global leader in the design, manufacture and distribution of branded home improvement and building products. Our portfolio of industry-leading brands includes BEHR® paint; DELTA® and HANSGROHE® faucets, bath and shower fixtures; LIBERTY® branded decorative and functional hardware; and HOT SPRING® spas. We leverage our powerful brands across product categories, sales channels and geographies to create value for our customers and shareholders. We believe that our solid results of operations and financial position for 2025 resulted from our continued focus on our strategy to drive the full potential of our core businesses, leverage opportunities across our enterprise, and actively manage our portfolio. In 2025, we continued to return value to our shareholders by repurchasing approximately 8.5 million shares of our common stock and increasing our quarterly dividend by approximately seven percent compared to 2024.

analysis_md:
# MAS — Masco Corporation
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-17. All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Branded home-improvement and building products: Plumbing Products (Delta, Peerless, Brizo, BrassCraft faucets/fittings, Hansgrohe, Watkins Wellness / Hot Spring spas) and Decorative Architectural Products (Behr and Kilz paints sold exclusively through Home Depot in North America, Liberty Hardware — being integrated into Delta Faucet from 2026). Demand is mostly repair-and-remodel of an aging US housing stock, so it is cyclical but not new-construction-dependent. Market cap $15.303B at $72.87 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,022,000,000; capex $156,000,000; SBC $30,000,000 (always a real cost; here it is small — 2.9% of OCF).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $836,000,000 = $3.98/share** (3.980952380952381 in dcf_numbers.json).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $726,000,000 — below the conservative figure, so the conservative base is not flattered by the maintenance definition; the gap is working capital and the capex/D&A relationship, noted under BASE notes below.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. OE/share history: 2021 $2.95, 2022 $2.44, 2023 $5.04, 2024 $3.96, 2025 $3.98. The 2023 print is an OCF spike ($1,413,000,000 OCF that year vs $1,022,000,000 in FY2025), not a run rate.
- **Base used = median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $3.98/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The median and the latest FY are the same $3.98 because 2024 ($3.96) and 2025 ($3.98) sit either side of it and the 2023 spike ($5.04) is the high outlier the median correctly ignores. No TTM base and no base_override: see STALE_FY below.
- Balance sheet (dcf_numbers.json / financials_history.csv): net debt $2,300,000,000 (LongTermDebtNoncurrent + NotesPayableCurrent basis), lease liabilities $268,000,000, cash $647,000,000, equity −$185,000,000 (negative because of decades of buybacks, not operating losses — net income was $810,000,000 in FY2025). Net debt is 2.75x normalized OE (diagnostics: net_debt_to_normalized_oe 2.751196172248804). Shares: diluted 210,000,000 (FY2025 weighted); shares outstanding 201,734,437 as of 2026-03-31.

## MOAT: 7/10 — strong, not wide
Justification: leading branded positions with pro-channel preference and proven pricing power, on ROIC that stayed far above the cost of capital through a downturn; capped by shelf-level substitutability, Home Depot concentration, and cyclicality the brands could not offset.
- Evidence (fundamentals.json, annual): **ROIC proxy** (after-tax operating income over equity + debt − cash) was 0.5265 (2021), 0.4434 (2022), 0.4777 (2023), 0.5042 (2024), 0.4461 (2025) — 44-53% every year, including the 2022-25 revenue decline. Caveat in words: the denominator is small because buybacks have driven book equity negative, so the level is flattered by the capital structure; the *persistence through a cycle* is the real signal. **Gross margin:** 34.19% (2021), 31.26% (2022), 35.60% (2023), 36.17% (2024), 35.43% (2025) — held and recovered while revenue fell, i.e. pricing offset volume.
- FOR: ROIC proxy 0.44-0.53 every year 2021-25, well above cost of capital through a downturn; Behr paint's exclusive Home Depot distribution since 1978 and Delta/Hansgrohe pro-channel preference; proven pricing power — gross margin held 31.3-36.2% and expanded in Q2 2026 while volumes fell; #1/#2 branded positions (Delta, Behr, Hansgrohe, Hot Spring) in repair-and-remodel categories driven by an aging housing stock.
- AGAINST: no real switching costs — DIY consumers can switch paint/faucet brands at the shelf (Sherwin-Williams, Moen, Kohler, private label); customer concentration — Behr sells exclusively through Home Depot in North America; housing and R&R cyclicality — revenue fell from $8,680,000,000 (2022) to $7,562,000,000 (2025) despite the brands; tariff and commodity exposure on imported plumbing components and paint inputs.
- A 7 gives CAP = 11.1 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 11.1 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (engine 5.4.0, 2026-10-17)
The engine's blended growth start is −0.68% (g_blend −0.0067889062826824165): revenue CAGR 5y +1.02%, 3y −4.49%, latest FY YoY −3.40%, OE/share CAGR 2y −11.12% (that last leg is measured off the 2023 OCF spike, so it overstates the decline); the revenue legs are credited +3.27pp for the shrinking share count (share_cagr −3.27%/yr).

**Growth recalibration (written reason):** the blend describes the 2022-25 down-leg, not the current print set. Latest FY revenue was −3.40%, but Q1 2026 revenue grew +6.5% YoY and Q2 2026 fell −3% YoY ($1,992 million, company release 2026-07-29), H1 was modestly positive, and management guided 2026 sales up low single digits with adjusted EPS guidance raised to $4.40-$4.60 (from $4.10-$4.30) on 2026-07-29 — partly an estimated $85 million net tariff refund, a one-off, so EPS growth overstates OE growth. With the share count shrinking ~3-4%/yr, a sales path of roughly flat-to-low-single-digits supports OE/share growth of about +3% as the base start. Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.0832 / −0.0132 / +0.0368 / +0.0768 / +0.1268 vs g_base) to −9 / −2 / **+3** / +7 / +12%. Sanity check against prints: the base start (+3% OE/share) sits above the latest FY revenue print (−3.40%) for the stated reasons (guidance, buyback, H1 stabilization) and below Q1 2026's EPS growth; the bull start (+7%) requires the guided sales growth plus operating leverage, not a housing boom; super bull (+12%) is the only start that needs a real R&R rebound, and it carries just 10% probability. Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 (defaults unchanged). Price $72.87.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −9.0% | 0.75 | R&R downturn deepens, tariffs/commodities bite, pricing gives back | $14.33 | 4.47% |
| Bear | 25% | −2.0% | 0.90 | Sales keep sliding at the recent pace, margins hold only partly | $23.79 | 6.34% |
| Base | 30% | +3.0% | 1.00 | Guided low-single-digit sales + buyback carry OE/share | $33.42 | 8.26% |
| Bull | 25% | +7.0% | 1.10 | R&R stabilizes, pricing + pro-paint share gains, operating leverage | $44.43 | 10.33% |
| Super bull | 10% | +12.0% | 1.25 | Full housing/R&R rebound off the aging housing stock | $64.01 | 13.64% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $34.91 (−52.1% vs price), IV@12% $46.28, IV@10% $58.96, weighted IRR 8.60%, base-case IRR 8.26%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Bear tier D (6.34%), bull tier C (10.33%). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 5.46%, terminal value 18.6% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.47x, net debt 2.75x normalized OE, 9.5 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (dcf_numbers.json): clears 15% at $34.91, 20% at $24.70, 25% at $19.07. At $72.87 even the super-bull IV@15% ($64.01) is below the price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): ttm.py was run and exits non-zero — it cannot compute TTM for MAS because SBC has no post-FY YTD fact (Masco does not file SBC in its 10-Qs; SBC is only in the annual history, $30,000,000 in FY2025). No --ttm base was used and no base_override was declared: the substitute evidence is fundamentals.json's filing-direct TTM through 2026-03-31 — revenue $7,679,000,000, operating income $1,278,000,000, OCF $1,101,000,000, capex $158,000,000, FCF $943,000,000, FCF/share $4.54, gross margin 35.42% — which runs modestly above the FY2025 base year and does not contradict the median base of $3.98/share, so the median base stands. The Q2 2026 10-Q (period 2026-06-30, filed 2026-07-29) is not yet in EDGAR companyfacts per fundamentals.json's warning, so filing-direct TTM stops at 2026-03-31; Q2 color above comes from the company's 2026-07-29 release, cited as such.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 3.3%/yr): already credited via the +3.27pp growth adjustment on the revenue components of the blend (share_adj_basis: applied to revenue components only, v5.4); the scenario recalibration also counts the buyback once, in the base-start reasoning — not double-counted in the verdict. The board authorized a new $2.0 billion repurchase program on 2026-02-10 (company release), and $454 million was returned in H1 2026 (Q2 2026 release).
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.47x super-bear IV): real — the range is the housing cycle, from a deepening R&R downturn to a full rebound. Confidence is capped at medium, and the verdict is sized to the conservative end (bear/base).
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D at 6.34% vs bull tier C at 10.33%): the verdict spans tiers; sized to the bear end — the final tier is D on the weighted 8.60%, and even the bull end only reaches C.

## My thoughts / overlay
- Quality is not the debate: this is a high-ROIC, pricing-power franchise that held gross margin and ~$0.8-1.1B of annual owner's earnings through a three-year revenue decline, pays a dividend (DPS TTM $1.25, fundamentals.json) and buys back ~3-4% of the count a year. The debate is price: at $72.87 the market is paying for the R&R recovery before it has shown up in revenue — the weighted IV@15% is $34.91 and the super-bull case ($64.01) still does not reach the price.
- Method range: on the preliminary default run (moat 5, blend growth −0.68% with default offsets) the weighted IRR was 7.75% and IV@15% $30.80 — also Tier D. The final run's friendlier growth recalibration and moat 7 move the answer to 8.60% / $34.91, still solidly D. Every defensible method tried here lands in D; there is no C-or-better method in this run.
- Watch items: the Q2 2026 gross-margin jump (43.6% reported, +600bp YoY, per the company release) includes tariff-refund effects — do not annualize it; the $85 million estimated net tariff refund inside raised FY2026 guidance is a one-off; Behr's Home Depot exclusivity is both the moat and the concentration risk; Liberty Hardware's integration into Delta changes segment reporting from 2026, a comparability break for segment-level work in pass 2.
- Data note (enrichment): all six enrichment steps completed (fundamentals, prices, segments, statements, profile, reprice). fundamentals.json and statements.py both warn the Q2 2026 10-Q is not yet in EDGAR companyfacts, so filing-direct quarterly rows stop at 2026-03-31.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.60%; bear D, bull C — sized to the conservative end)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the base — median and latest FY agree at $3.98 and OE was positive 5/5 years; capped by the 4.47x scenario spread and the TTM/SBC filing gap)
- One-liner: High-quality branded building-products franchise, moat 7/10 — does not clear 15% at $72.87 (weighted IRR 8.6%, weighted IV@15% $34.91); it clears 15% only at or below $34.91, and even the bull case is just 10.3%.
